title: Draw a contour or density only for experts, with its smoothing stated.
rule: Use contours or a density surface, a reference form, to show where very many points concentrate on two measures: draw lines of equal density, like a map’s height lines, or shade bands between them, and state the smoothing. Draw the few points that matter on top.
use_when: A specialist asks where the bulk of very many records lies on two measures, and the exact counts matter less than the shape.

use_instead.when: Counts a reader can check in each area
A few dozen points the reader can name

text: Contours draw a dense cloud’s shape as lines, so points the story names can sit on top and stay readable. The smoothing changes the shape, so the reader needs to know it.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: No kit form: draw density contours in a specialist piece, from a density the analyst states.
sketch_alt: Three nested contour rings around the densest part of a point cloud, the inner ring darkest, with a few points outside the outer ring.
